$schema_note: Not a formal JSON-Schema file, just documenting the shape here: each entry has id, displayName, kind (own-product | third-party-trademark), guidelinesUrl, source, file, lastVerified. 'pending' entries are documented gaps, not usable assets: they have no 'file' because no verified official SVG has been fetched yet, per assets/logos/README.md rule 1 (never fabricate a brand's logo).

source.note: Project owner's own product logo, copied from the cutepi repo. Not a third-party trademark, not covered by an external brand-guidelines page.
Alternate treatment of the cutepi logo, copied from the cutepi repo. Same ownership/licensing status as 'cutepi'.
Project owner's own product logo, copied from the playlist-lab repo. Not a third-party trademark.

Real trademark, not vendored: needs YouTube's own official SVG fetched from a verified youtube.com/google brand-resources page with the guidelines URL confirmed, or an owner-supplied file with confirmed rights. Tabler's brand-* set is hard-excluded from the generic icon pack for the same reason — use this logos/ system, not assets/icons/, for the mark. An integrator that can't wait self-hosts per assets/logos/README.md ('Self-hosting a third-party mark') without touching this manifest.

playlist-lab's static/service-logos/spotify.svg exists in the sibling repo but was deliberately NOT copied here — that copy's provenance/rights are playlist-lab's own concern, not this shared library's to redistribute. Needs either (a) Spotify's own official SVG fetched from a verified spotify.com/developer.spotify.com brand-resources page with the guidelines URL recorded, or (b) the project owner explicitly supplying a file they hold rights to use. Do not add a 'file' field until one of those happens. .btn-brand.is-spotify (core/components/surfaces.css) ships the colours and spacing only; Spotify's design page (2026-10-02) ties its logo downloads to accepting the Developer Terms, so apps self-host the icon.

Same situation as spotify above: real trademark, not vendored. Needs Apple's own official identity-guidelines asset fetched from a verified apple.com page, or an owner-supplied file with confirmed rights.
Real trademark, not vendored. No official brand-guidelines URL confirmed yet — needs research to find Amazon's official brand-asset page before any SVG or guidelines link is added here.

Fetched 2026-10-02 from Google's own developers.google.com branding page, which offers these pre-approved assets for Sign in with Google buttons. File = 'Android + Web/SVG/Light/Theme=Light, Show text=No, Shape=Square, Platform=Android+Web.svg' with the two button-frame paths removed and the viewBox cropped to the 20x20 logo area; the G itself is unchanged (the guidelines say custom-size logos start from the bundle's files). Only for Sign in with Google buttons (.btn-brand.is-google), at the fixed size those guidelines set; any other use needs Google's written consent.

Fetched 2026-10-02 from Microsoft's own learn.microsoft.com branding page ('To download the official Microsoft logo for use in your app...'). Byte-identical copy. Only for Sign in with Microsoft buttons (.btn-brand.is-microsoft); don't alter the logo.

Not vendored. GitHub's logo page permits using the Invertocat to show integration, but its legal section says no use 'of any kind' without GitHub's express written permission, which gives this shared library no redistribution right. Apps self-host the mark from https://brand.github.com/GitHub_Logos.zip (white on dark, black on light) and pass it to .btn-brand.is-github as .

Not vendored. The HIG requires the logo artwork to come from Apple Design Resources (https://developer.apple.com/design/resources/), which is downloaded by each developer under Apple's terms; nothing on the page grants redistribution. Apps download the 'logo and text' artwork themselves and pass it to .btn-brand.is-apple as (the file's built-in padding is required; don't crop it).
